title: Trustworthy Telemetry and Event Design
editorial_note: Automated dialogue draft from the revised lesson. Review spoken wording and meaning before publishing.

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Today we're talking about Trustworthy Telemetry and Event Design. By the end, you'll know why this matters, how to use it, and what to notice in a real product.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What is the problem we are trying to understand?

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Telemetry is instrumentation that records product and system behaviour for defined decisions. An event name is not evidence until its trigger and semantics are explicit.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What changes when we look at events are claims about state?

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Model the domain before naming events. Distinguish:

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: intent from attempt; client display from actual exposure; request from server acceptance; pending from completion; failure from cancellation; retry from a new instance; recovery from silent abandonment.

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: For each event define actor, entity, state transition, trigger, authoritative source, client or server timestamp, experiment assignment, schema version, required properties, allowed values, identity and join keys, deduplication, privacy classification, owner, and quality tests.

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Client telemetry can show what was rendered and interacted with but may be lost through navigation, blocking, offline use, or device failure. Server telemetry is generally more reliable for processing states but cannot prove what a person saw or understood. Reconcile streams through stable identifiers and clear source authority.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What changes when we look at design an event contract?

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Begin with the behaviour and causal model, not every clickable element. Instrument states needed to test decisions and diagnose important paths. Clickstream detail without semantic state produces volume without understanding.

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: An event contract includes:

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: business meaning and non-meaning; exact emission condition and emitting system; entity lifecycle and legal transitions; properties, types, null rules, and units; identity, consent, and cross-device rules; latency and late-arrival expectations; retry/idempotency behaviour; versioning and migration policy; tests, monitors, owner, and downstream consumers.

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: When meaning changes, version the event or metric. Do not silently retain a name and rewrite history.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What changes when we look at transfer example: identity verification?

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: An event called verificationfailed might mean document rejected, camera unavailable, server timeout, user cancelled, or session expired. Combining them produces an alarming but unactionable rate. A state model separates user intent, technical attempt, vendor response, retry, recovery, and final verified outcome while avoiding storage of document content.

turns.speaker: host
turns.act: Data quality is a live product responsibility
turns.text: What changes when we look at data quality is a live product responsibility?

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Monitor completeness, duplication, freshness, validity, consistency, and distribution. Compare client and server signals, reconcile source-of-truth totals, and investigate impossible transitions. Broken instrumentation deserves incident priority because teams operating blind can expose people to undetected harm.

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Document known gaps beside dashboards. A data pipeline being available does not mean the measurement is trustworthy.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What changes when we look at where this can go wrong?

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Visible-is-fired: exposure records control availability rather than actual encounter. State compression: attempt and fulfilled outcome share one “complete” label. Client-only truth: lossy interface logs represent server or service outcome. Schema drift: releases change meaning without versioning.

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Identity collision: people, accounts, referrals, sessions, and attempts are joined incorrectly. Overcollection: sensitive content is captured without a justified decision. Dashboard-first instrumentation: charts precede domain semantics and quality tests.

turns.speaker: host
turns.act: Treat telemetry as a governed product model
turns.text: What changes when we look at treat telemetry as a governed product model?

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: The tracking plan begins with decisions and measures. Every event states which question it supports and what it cannot observe. Page views do not reveal comprehension; button clicks do not prove intention; missing events can mean technical loss or no behaviour.

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Server events are preferred for authoritative service state, while client events can describe interaction if consent and reliability are appropriate.

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Quality controls detect duplicate events, missing properties, impossible sequences, version drift, bot or test traffic, sample-ratio anomalies, and delayed ingestion. Engineers validate against real case histories before release. Data contracts and ownership make breaking changes visible, and historical dashboards record definition shifts.

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Privacy uses minimisation, purpose limitation, access control, retention, and review. Sensitive clinical content is not copied into analytics because it may be useful later. Debugging identifiers are separated and protected. Trustworthy telemetry acknowledges the people it cannot observe and remains paired with direct and operational research.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What changes when we look at transfer example: checkout?

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: purchaseclicked is not a purchase. Authorisation, order creation, inventory reservation, fulfilment, cancellation, and refund have different sources and consequences. A governed event model prevents conversion from being counted before value exists.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Where does the harder design decision appear?

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Instrumentation determines whose behaviour becomes legible and which states disappear. Senior designers help define event semantics because telemetry will later be treated as a description of experience.

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Establish a cross-functional catalogue, review instrumentation in design and code changes, give broken data feature-level priority, and fund deletion and migration—not only collection.

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: <! -- Editorial: manual revision; curated product example --

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Can we see that in a concrete product situation?

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Illustrative scenario: a delivery app. An event called “ordercomplete” fires both when payment succeeds and when a confirmation screen loads from cache. The metric cannot support decisions until its meaning is repaired. Specify event names, triggers, identifiers, missing-data checks, and privacy limits so telemetry corresponds to the behaviour the team claims to measure.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What should I notice the next time I use a product?

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Open an analytics event list if you have access. Select a name such as submitted or active. Can two teams independently infer the same trigger, entity, and outcome? If not, the event is ambiguous evidence.
